summary: Encodes up to a2 bytes from input buffer a1 into base64, writing to output buffer a3 and null-terminating it. Bytes are consumed in groups of three; a partial trailing group is zero-padded before the four base64 characters are produced via Base64IndexToCharEncoding.

operations.description: If a2 <= 0, skip encoding entirely, write a single null terminator into a3 and return.
Outer while loop repeats until the number of consumed input bytes v4 reaches the limit v12 (equal to a2).
Inner for loop gathers up to three input bytes into a temporary buffer; when fewer than three remain (v4 >= v3) the remaining slots are zero-filled to pad the group.
Pack the three gathered bytes into four 6-bit base64 indices (v10[0..3]) via shifts and masks on the 24-bit group.
For each of the four indices, call Base64IndexToCharEncoding(index) and write the returned character into the output buffer v5.
Advance the consumed-byte counter v4 by 3 per group; terminate the outer loop once v4 >= v12.
Write a null terminator after the last emitted base64 character (*v5 = 0).
Return the last character produced by Base64IndexToCharEncoding (the `result` variable reused by the decompiler).

unresolved: The canonical name 'PadOutputWithSpacesUpToLengthLimit' and the abi lead describe space padding, while the observed logic is base64 encoding; the output-consumer contract (caller sub_562E30) decides which framing applies.
Zero-padding a partial group yields base64 characters for the zero bytes; whether the caller expects '=' padding or trailing spaces is unresolved.
The decompiler reuses a1 and result as scratch registers; exact register-level grouping order is a compiler artifact.
